sermons.mainText: ‘They shall feed in the ways, and their pastures shall be in all high places.’—ISAIAH xlix. 9.

sermons.title: The Mountain Road
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.iii; heading #ii.ii.iii-p0.2 'THE MOUNTAIN ROAD'
sermons.mainText: ‘And I will make all My mountains a way, and My highways shall be exalted.’—ISAIAH xlix. 11.

sermons.title: The Writing on God’s Hands
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.iv; heading #ii.ii.iv-p0.2 'THE WRITING ON GOD’S HANDS'
sermons.mainText: ‘Behold! I have graven thee upon the palms of My hands; thy walls are continually before Me.’—ISAIAH xlix. 16.

sermons.title: The Servant’s Words to the Weary
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.v; heading #ii.ii.v-p0.2 'THE SERVANT’S WORDS TO THE WEARY'
sermons.mainText: ‘The Lord God hath given me the tongue of them that are taught, that I should know how to sustain with words him that is weary; he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as they that are taught.’—ISAIAH l. 4.

sermons.title: The Servant’s Obedience
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.vi; heading #ii.ii.vi-p0.2 'THE SERVANT’S OBEDIENCE'
sermons.mainText: ‘I was not rebellious, neither turned away back’—ISAIAH l. 5.

sermons.title: The Servant’s Voluntary Sufferings
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.vii; heading #ii.ii.vii-p0.2 'THE SERVANT’S VOLUNTARY SUFFERINGS'
sermons.mainText: ‘I gave My back to the smiters, and My cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not My face from shame and spitting.’—ISAIAH l. 6.

sermons.title: The Servant’s Inflexible Resolve
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.viii; heading #ii.ii.viii-p0.2 'THE SERVANT’S INFLEXIBLE RESOLVE'
sermons.mainText: ‘For the Lord God will help Me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set My face like a flint.’—ISAIAH l. 7.

sermons.title: The Servant’s Triumph
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.ix; heading #ii.ii.ix-p0.2 'THE SERVANT’S TRIUMPH'
sermons.mainText: ‘He is near that justifieth Me; who will contend with Me? let us stand together: who is Mine adversary? let him come near to Me. 9. Behold, the Lord God will help Me; who is he that shall condemn Me? lo, they all shall wax old as a garment; the moth shall eat them up.’—ISAIAH l. 8, 9.

sermons.title: A Call to Faith
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.x; heading #ii.ii.x-p0.2 'A CALL TO FAITH'
sermons.mainText: ‘Who is among you that feareth the Lord, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the Lord, and stay upon his God.’—ISAIAH l. 10.

sermons.title: Dying Fire
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xi; heading #ii.ii.xi-p0.2 'DYING FIRES'
sermons.mainText: ‘Behold, all ye that kindle a fire, that gird yourselves about with firebrands: walk ye in the flame of your fire, and among the brands that ye have kindled. This shall ye have of mine hand; ye shall lie down in sorrow.’—ISAIAH l. 11.

sermons.title: The Awakening of Zion
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xii; heading #ii.ii.xii-p0.2 'THE AWAKENING OF ZION'
sermons.mainText:
‘Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the Lord; awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old.’—ISAIAH li. 9.
‘Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion.’—ISAIAH lii. 1.

sermons.title: A Pardox of Selling and Buying
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xiii; heading #ii.ii.xiii-p0.2 'A PARADOX OF SELLING AND BUYING'
sermons.mainText: ‘Ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money.’—ISAIAH lii. 3.

sermons.title: Clean Carriers
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xiv; heading #ii.ii.xiv-p0.2 'CLEAN CARRIERS'
sermons.mainText: ‘Be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the Lord.’—ISAIAH lii. 11.

sermons.title: Marching Orders
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xv; heading #ii.ii.xv-p0.2 'MARCHING ORDERS'
sermons.mainText: ‘Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the Lord. 12. For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the Lord will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your reward.’—ISAIAH lii. 11, 12.

sermons.title: The Arm of the Lord
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xvi; heading #ii.ii.xvi-p0.2 'THE ARM OF THE LORD'
sermons.mainText: ‘To whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?’—ISAIAH liii 1.

sermons.title: The Suffering Servant—I
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xvii; heading #ii.ii.xvii-p0.2 'THE SUFFERING SERVANT—I'
sermons.mainText: ‘For He grew up before Him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground He hath no form nor comeliness; and when we see Him, there is no beauty that we should desire Him. 3. He was despised, and rejected of men, a Man of Sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and as one from whom men hide their face He was despised, and we esteemed Him not.’—ISAIAH liii, 2, 3.

sermons.title: The Suffering Servant—II
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xviii; heading #ii.ii.xviii-p0.2 'THE SUFFERING SERVANT—II'
sermons.mainText: ‘Surely He hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem Him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. 5. But He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon Him; and with His stripes we are healed. 6. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord hath laid (made to light) on Him the iniquity of us all.’—ISAIAH liii. 4-6.

sermons.title: The Suffering Servant—III
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xix; heading #ii.ii.xix-p0.2 'THE SUFFERING SERVANT—III.'
sermons.mainText: ‘He was oppressed, yet He humbled Himself and opened not His mouth; as a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before her shearers is dumb; yea, He opened not His mouth. 8. By oppression and judgment He was taken away; and as for His generation, who among them considered that He was cut off out of the land of the living? for the transgression of my people was He stricken. 9. And they made His grave with the wicked, and with the rich in His death; although He had done no violence, neither was any deceit in His mouth’—ISAIAH liii, 7-9. R. V.

sermons.title: The Suffering Servant—IV
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xx; heading #ii.ii.xx-p0.2 'THE SUFFERING SERVANT—IV'
sermons.mainText: ‘It pleased the Lord to bruise Him; He hath put Him to grief: when Thou shalt make His soul an offering for sin, He shall see His seed, He shall prolong His days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in His hand.’—ISAIAH liii. 10.

sermons.title: The Suffering Servant—V
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxi; heading #ii.ii.xxi-p0.2 'THE SUFFERING SERVANT—V'
sermons.mainText: ‘He shall see of the travail of His soul, and shall be satisfied: by His knowledge shall My righteous servant justify many; and He shall bear their iniquities’—ISAIAH liii. 11.

sermons.title: The Suffering Servant—VI
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxii; heading #ii.ii.xxii-p0.2 'THE SUFFERING SERVANT—VI'
sermons.mainText: ‘Therefore will I divide Him a portion with the great, and He shall divide the spoil with the strong; because He hath poured out His soul unto death: and was numbered with the transgressors; and He bare the sins of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.’—ISAIAH liii. 12.

sermons.title: The Passing and the Permanent
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxiii; heading #ii.ii.xxiii-p0.2 'THE PASSING AND THE PERMANENT'
sermons.mainText: ‘For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but My kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of My peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee.’—ISAIAH liv, 10.

sermons.title: The Call to the Thirsty
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxiv; heading #ii.ii.xxiv-p0.2 'THE CALL TO THE THIRSTY'
sermons.mainText: ‘Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. 2. Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto Me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness. 3. Incline your ear, and come unto Me, hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David. 4. Behold, I have given him for a witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people. 5. Behold, thou shalt call a nation that thou knowest not, and nations that knew not thee shall run unto thee because of the Lord thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for He hath glorified thee. 6. Seek ye the Lord while He may be found, call ye upon Him while He is near: 7. Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and He will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for He will abundantly pardon. 8. For My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways, saith the Lord. 9. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are My ways higher than your ways, and My thoughts than your thoughts. 10. For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: 11. So shall My word be that goeth forth out of My mouth: it shall not return unto Me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it. 12. For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands. 13. Instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree: and it shall be to the Lord for a name, for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off.’—ISAIAH lv. 1-13.

sermons.title: The Great Proclamation
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxv; heading #ii.ii.xxv-p0.2 'THE GREAT PROCLAMATION'
sermons.mainText: ‘Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.’—ISAIAH lv. 1.

sermons.title: God’s Ways and Man’s
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxvi; heading #ii.ii.xxvi-p0.2 'GOD’S WAYS AND MAN’S'
sermons.mainText: ‘For My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways, saith the Lord. 9. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are My ways higher than your ways, and My thoughts than your thoughts.’—ISAIAH lv. 8, 9.

sermons.title: We Sure of To-morrow? A New Year’s Sermon
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxvii; heading #ii.ii.xxvii-p0.2 'WE SURE OF TO-MORROW? A NEW YEAR’S SERMON'
sermons.mainText: ‘To-morrow shall be as this day, and much more abundant.’—ISAIAH lvi. 12.

sermons.title: Flimsy Garments
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxviii; heading #ii.ii.xxviii-p0.2 'FLIMSY GARMENTS'
sermons.mainText:
‘Their webs shall not become garments.’—ISAIAH lix. 6.
‘I counsel thee to buy of me . . . white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear.’—REV. iii. 18.

sermons.title: The Sunlit Church
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxix; heading #ii.ii.xxix-p0.2 'THE SUNLIT CHURCH'
sermons.mainText: ‘Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee. 2. For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people; but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and His glory shall be seen upon thee. 3. And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.’—ISAIAH lx. 1-3.

sermons.title: Walls and Gates
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxx; heading #ii.ii.xxx-p0.2 'WALLS AND GATES'
sermons.mainText: ‘Thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise’—ISAIAH lx. 18.

sermons.title: The Joy-bringer
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxxi; heading #ii.ii.xxxi-p0.2 'THE JOY-BRINGER'
sermons.mainText: ‘To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness.’—ISAIAH lxi. 3.

sermons.title: The Heavenly Workers and the Earthly Watchers
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxxii; heading #ii.ii.xxxii-p0.2 'THE HEAVENLY WORKERS AND THE EARTHLY WATCHERS'
sermons.mainText: ‘For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest . . . I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, and give Him no rest’—ISAIAH lxii. 1, 6, 7.

sermons.title: Mighty to Save
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxxiii; heading #ii.ii.xxxiii-p0.2 'MIGHTY TO SAVE'
sermons.mainText: ‘Mighty to save.’—ISAIAH lxiii. 1.

sermons.title: The Winepress and Its Treader
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxxiv; heading #ii.ii.xxxiv-p0.2 'THE WINEPRESS AND ITS TREADER'
sermons.mainText: ‘Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat? I have trodden the winepress alone.’—ISAIAH lxiii. 2, 3.

sermons.title: The Sympathy of God
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxxv; heading #ii.ii.xxxv-p0.2 'THE SYMPATHY OF GOD'
sermons.mainText: ‘In all their afflictions He was afflicted, and the angel of His presence saved them’—ISAIAH lxiii. 9.

sermons.title: How to Meet God
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxxvi; heading #ii.ii.xxxvi-p0.2 'HOW TO MEET GOD'
sermons.mainText: ‘Thou meetest him that rejoiceth and worketh righteousness, those that remember Thee in Thy ways.’—ISAIAH lxiv. 5.

sermons.title: ‘The God of the Amen’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii.xxxvii; heading #ii.ii.xxxvii-p0.2 '‘THE GOD OF THE AMEN’'
sermons.mainText: ‘He who blesseth himself in the earth shall bless himself in the God of truth; and he that sweareth in the earth shall swear by the God of truth.’—ISAIAH lxv. 16.

sermons.title: God’s Lawsuit
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.i; heading #ii.iii.i-p0.2 'GOD’S LAWSUIT'
sermons.mainText: ‘Wherefore I will yet plead with you, saith the Lord, and with your children’s children will I plead.’—JER. ii. 9.

sermons.title: Stiff-necked Idolaters and Pliable Christians
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.ii; heading #ii.iii.ii-p0.2 'STIFF-NECKED IDOLATERS AND PLIABLE CHRISTIANS'
sermons.mainText: ‘Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but My people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.’—JER. ii. 11.

sermons.title: Fountain and Cistern
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.iii; heading #ii.iii.iii-p0.2 'FOUNTAIN AND CISTERNS'
sermons.mainText: ‘They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water’—JER. ii. 13.

sermons.title: Forsaking Jehovah
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.iv; heading #ii.iii.iv-p0.2 'FORSAKING JEHOVAH'
sermons.mainText: ‘Know therefore, and see, that it is an evil thing and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, and that My fear is not in thee, saith the Lord God of hosts.’—JER. ii. 19.

sermons.title: A Colloquy between a Penitent and God
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.v; heading #ii.iii.v-p0.2 'A COLLOQUY BETWEEN A PENITENT AND GOD'
sermons.mainText: ‘A voice was heard upon the high places, weeping and supplications of the children of Israel: for they have perverted their way, and they have forgotten the Lord their God. Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. Behold, we come unto Thee; for Thou art the Lord our God.’—JER. iii. 21, 22.

sermons.title: A Question for the Beginning
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.vi; heading #ii.iii.vi-p0.2 'A QUESTION FOR THE BEGINNING'
sermons.mainText: ‘What will ye do in the end?’—JER. v. 31.

sermons.title: Possessing and Possessed
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.vii; heading #ii.iii.vii-p0.2 'POSSESSING AND POSSESSED'
sermons.mainText: ‘The portion of Jacob is not like them—for He is the former of all things: and Israel is the tribe of His inheritance. The Lord of Hosts is His name.’—JER. x. 16, R.V.

sermons.title: Calms and Crises
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.viii; heading #ii.iii.viii-p0.2 'CALMS AND CRISES'
sermons.mainText: ‘If thou hast run with the footmen, and they have wearied thee, then how canst thou contend with horses? and though in a land of peace thou art secure, yet how wilt thou do in the pride of Jordan?’—JER. xii. 5, R.V.

sermons.title: An Impossibility Made Possible
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.ix; heading #ii.iii.ix-p0.2 'AN IMPOSSIBILITY MADE POSSIBLE'
sermons.mainText:
‘Can the Ethiopian change his skin?’—JER. xiii. 23.
‘If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature.’—2 COR. v. 17.
‘Behold, I make all things new.’—REV. xxi. 5.

sermons.title: Triumphant Prayer
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.x; heading #ii.iii.x-p0.2 'TRIUMPHANT PRAYER'
sermons.mainText: ‘O Lord, though our iniquities testify against us, do Thou it for Thy name’s sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against Thee. 8. O the hope of Israel, the saviour thereof in time of trouble, why shouldest Thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man that turneth aside to tarry for a night? 9. Why shouldest Thou be as a man astonied, as a mighty man that cannot save? yet Thou, O Lord, art in the midst of us, and we are called by Thy name; leave us not.’—JER. xiv. 7-9.

sermons.title: Sin’s Writing and Its Erasure
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xi; heading #ii.iii.xi-p0.2 'SIN’S WRITING AND ITS ERASURE'
sermons.mainText:
‘The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond: it is graven upon the table of their heart, and upon the horns of your altars.’—JER. xvii. 1.
‘Ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.’—2 COR. iii. 3.
‘Blotting out the handwriting that was against us.’—COL. ii. 14.

sermons.title: The Heath in the Desert and the Tree by the River
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xii; heading #ii.iii.xii-p0.2 'THE HEATH IN THE DESERT AND THE TREE BY THE RIVER'
sermons.mainText: ‘He shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh; but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, a salt land and not inhabited. . . He shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.’—JER. xvii. 6, 8.

sermons.title: A Soul Gazing on God
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xiii; heading #ii.iii.xiii-p0.2 'A SOUL GAZING ON GOD'
sermons.mainText: ‘A glorious high throne from the beginning is the place of our sanctuary.’—JER. xvii. 12.

sermons.title: Two Lists of Names
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xiv; heading #ii.iii.xiv-p0.2 'TWO LISTS OF NAMES'
sermons.mainText:
‘They that depart from Me shall be written in the earth’—JER. xvii. 13.
‘Rejoice that your names are written in heaven.’—LUKE x. 20.

sermons.title: Yokes of Wood and Iron
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xv; heading #ii.iii.xv-p0.2 'YOKES OF WOOD AND IRON'
sermons.mainText: ‘Go and tell Hananiah, saying, Thus saith the Lord; Thou hast broken the yokes of wood; but thou shalt make for them yokes of iron.’—JER. xxviii. 13.

sermons.title: What the Stable Creation Teaches
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xvi; heading #ii.iii.xvi-p0.2 'WHAT THE STABLE CREATION TEACHES'
sermons.mainText: ‘If those ordinances depart from before Me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before Me for ever.’—JER. xxxi. 36.

sermons.title: What the Immense Creation Teaches
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xvii; heading #ii.iii.xvii-p0.2 'WHAT THE IMMENSE CREATION TEACHES'
sermons.mainText: ‘If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done, saith the Lord.’—JER. xxxi. 37.

sermons.title: A Threefold Disease and a Twofold Cure
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xviii; heading #ii.iii.xviii-p0.2 'A THREEFOLD DISEASE AND A TWOFOLD CURE.'
sermons.mainText: ‘I will cleanse them from all their iniquity, whereby they have sinned against Me; and I will pardon all their iniquities, whereby they have sinned, and whereby they have transgressed against Me.’—JER. xxxiii. 8.

sermons.title: The Rechabites
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xix; heading #ii.iii.xix-p0.2 'THE RECHABITES'
sermons.mainText: ‘The sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have performed the commandment of their father, which he commanded them; but this people have not hearkened unto Me.’—JER. xxxv. 16.

sermons.title: Jeremiah’s Roll Burned and Reproduced
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xx; heading #ii.iii.xx-p0.2 'JEREMIAH’S ROLL BURNED AND REPRODUCED'
sermons.mainText: ‘Then took Jeremiah another roll, and gave it to Baruch . . . who wrote therein . . . all the words of the book which Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire, and there were added besides unto them many like words.’—JER. xxxvi. 32.

sermons.title: Zedekiah
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xxi; heading #ii.iii.xxi-p0.2 'ZEDEKIAH'
sermons.mainText: ‘Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned as king . . . whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king’—JER. xxxvii. 1.

sermons.title: The World’s Wages to a Prophet
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xxii; heading #ii.iii.xxii-p0.2 'THE WORLD’S WAGES TO A PROPHET'
sermons.mainText: ‘And it came to pass, that when the army of the Chaldeans was broken up from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh’s arm, 12. Then Jeremiah went forth out of Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin, to separate himself thence in the midst of the people. 13. And when he was in the gate of Benjamin, a captain of the ward was there, whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he took Jeremiah the prophet, saying, Thou fallest away to the Chaldeans. 14. Then said Jeremiah, It is false; I fall not away to the Chaldeans. But he hearkened not to him: so Irijah took Jeremiah, and brought him to the princes. 15. Wherefore the princes were wroth with Jeremiah, and smote him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe: for they had made that the prison. 16. When Jeremiah was entered into the dungeon, and into the cabins, and Jeremiah had remained there many days; 17. Then Zedekiah the king sent, and took him out: and the king asked him secretly in his house, and said, Is there any word from the Lord? And Jeremiah said, There is: for, said he, thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon. 18. Moreover, Jeremiah said unto king Zedekiah, What have I offended against thee, or against thy servants, or against this people, that ye have put me in prison? 19. Where are now your prophets which prophesied unto you, saying, The king of Babylon shall not come against you, nor against this land? 20. Therefore hear now, I pray thee, O my lord the king: let my supplication, I pray thee, be accepted before thee; that thou cause me not to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there. 21. Then Zedekiah the king commanded that they should commit Jeremiah into the court of the prison, and that they should give him daily a piece of bread out of the bakers’ street, until all the bread in the city were spent. Thus Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.’—JER. xxxvii. 11-21.

sermons.title: The Last Agony
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xxiii; heading #ii.iii.xxiii-p0.2 'THE LAST AGONY'
sermons.mainText: ‘In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army against Jerusalem, and they besieged it. 2. And in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month, the city was broken up. 3. And all the princes of the king of Babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, even Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarse-chim, Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer, Rab-mag, with all the residue of the princes of the king of Babylon. 4. And it came to pass, that when Zedekiah the king of Judah saw them, and all the men of war, then they fled, and went forth out of the city by night, by the way of the king’s garden, by the gate betwixt the two walls: and he went out the way of the plain. 5. But the Chaldeans’ army pursued after them, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he gave judgment upon him. 6. Then the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes: also the king of Babylon slew all the nobles of Judah. 7. Moreover he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, and bound him with chains, to carry him to Babylon. 8. And the Chaldeans burned the king’s house, and the houses of the people, with fire, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem. 9. Then Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away captive into Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to him, with the rest of the people that remained. 10. But Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.’—JER. xxxix. 1-10.

sermons.title: Ebedmelech the Ethiopian
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xxiv; heading #ii.iii.xxiv-p0.2 'EBEDMELECH THE ETHIOPIAN'
sermons.mainText: ‘For I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in Me, saith the Lord.’—JER. xxxix. 18.

sermons.title: God’s Patient Pleadings
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xxv; heading #ii.iii.xxv-p0.2 'GOD’S PATIENT PLEADINGS'
sermons.mainText: ‘I sent unto you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying, Oh, do not this abominable thing that I hate.’—JER. xliv. 4.

sermons.title: The Sword of the Lord
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xxvi; heading #ii.iii.xxvi-p0.2 'THE SWORD OF THE LORD'
sermons.mainText: ‘O thou sword of the Lord, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still. 7. How can it be quiet, seeing the Lord hath given it a charge?’—JER. xlvii. 6, 7.

sermons.title: The Kinsman-redeemer
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xxvii; heading #ii.iii.xxvii-p0.2 'THE KINSMAN-REDEEMER'
sermons.mainText: ‘Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of Hosts is His name: He shall thoroughly plead their cause.’—JER. l. 34.

sermons.title: ‘As Sodom’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: Isaiah and Jeremiah (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii.xxviii; heading #ii.iii.xxviii-p0.2 '‘AS SODOM’'
sermons.mainText: ‘Zedekiah was one and twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah. 2. And he did that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done. 3. For through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, till he had cast them out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. 4. And it came to pass, in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it, and built forts against it round about. 5. So the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah. 6. And in the fourth month, in the ninth day of the month, the famine was sore in the city, so that there was no bread for the people of the land. 7. Then the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled, and went forth out of the city by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden; (now the Chaldeans were by the city round about) and they went by the way of the plain. 8. But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him. 9. Then they took the king, and carried him up unto the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; where he gave judgment upon him. 10. And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah. 11. Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death.’—JER. lii. 1-11.

sermons.title: The Word in Eternity, in the World, and in the Flesh
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii; heading #ii.ii-p0.2 'THE WORD IN ETERNITY, IN THE WORLD, AND IN THE FLESH'
sermons.mainText: ‘In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. 2. The same was in the beginning with God. 3. All things were made by Him; and without Him was not any thing made that was made. 4. In Him was life; and the life was the light of men. 5. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not. 6. There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. 7. The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe. 8. He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light. 9. That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world. 10. He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not. 11. He came unto His own, and His own received Him not. 12. But as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on His name: 13. Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. 14. And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only-begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.’—JOHN i. 1-14.

sermons.title: The Light and the Lamps
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii; heading #ii.iii-p0.2 'THE LIGHT AND THE LAMPS'
sermons.mainText: ‘He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light.’—JOHN i. 8.

sermons.title: ‘Three Tabernacles’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iv; heading #ii.iv-p0.2 '‘THREE TABERNACLES’'
sermons.mainText:
‘The Word . . . dwelt among us.’—JOHN i. 14.
‘ . . . He that sitteth on the Throne shall dwell among them.’—REV. vii. 15.
‘ . . . Behold, the Tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them.’—REV. xxi. 3.

sermons.title: The Fulness of Christ
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.v; heading #ii.v-p0.2 'THE FULNESS OF CHRIST'
sermons.mainText: ‘And of His fulness have all we received, and grace for grace.’—JOHN i. 16.

sermons.title: Grace and Truth
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.vi; heading #ii.vi-p0.2 'GRACE AND TRUTH'
sermons.mainText: ‘The law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.’—JOHN i. 17.

sermons.title: The World’s Sin-bearer
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.vii; heading #ii.vii-p0.2 'THE WORLD’S SIN-BEARER'
sermons.mainText: ‘The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.’—JOHN i. 29.

sermons.title: The First Disciples: I. John and Andrew
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.viii; heading #ii.viii-p0.2 'THE FIRST DISCIPLES: I. JOHN AND ANDREW'
sermons.mainText: ‘And the two disciples heard Him speak, and they followed Jesus. 38. Then Jesus turned, and saw them following, and saith unto them, What seek ye? They said unto Him, Rabbi, (which is to say, being interpreted, Master,) where dwellest Thou? 39. He saith unto them, Come and see. They came and saw where He dwelt, and abode with Him that day: for it was about the tenth hour.’—JOHN i. 37-39.

sermons.title: The First Disciples: II. Simon Peter
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ix; heading #ii.ix-p0.2 'THE FIRST DISCIPLES: II. SIMON PETER'
sermons.mainText: ‘One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother. 41. He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ. 42. And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, He said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is, by interpretation, a stone.’—JOHN i. 40-42.

sermons.title: The First Disciples: III. Philip
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.x; heading #ii.x-p0.2 'THE FIRST DISCIPLES: III. PHILIP'
sermons.mainText: ‘The day following Jesus would go forth into Galilee, and findeth Philip, and saith unto him, Follow Me.’—JOHN i. 43.

sermons.title: The First Disciples: IV. Nathanael
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xi; heading #ii.xi-p0.2 'THE FIRST DISCIPLES: IV. NATHANAEL'
sermons.mainText: ‘Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found Him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph. 46. And Nathanael said unto him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see. 47. Jesus saw Nathanael coming to Him, and saith of him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile! 48. Nathanael saith unto Him, Whence knowest Thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee. 49. Nathanael answered and saith unto Him, Rabbi, Thou art the Son of God; Thou art the King of Israel.’—JOHN i. 45-49.

sermons.title: The First Disciples: V. Believing and Seeing
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xii; heading #ii.xii-p0.2 'THE FIRST DISCIPLES: V. BELIEVING AND SEEING'
sermons.mainText: ‘Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto thee, I saw thee under the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these. 51. And He saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.’—JOHN i. 50, 51.

sermons.title: Jesus the Joy-bringer
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xiii; heading #ii.xiii-p0.2 'JESUS THE JOY-BRINGER'
sermons.mainText: ‘And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there: 2. And both Jesus was called, and His disciples, to the marriage. 3. And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus saith unto Him, They have no wine. 4. Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? Mine hour is not yet come. 5. His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever He saith unto you, do it. 6. And there were set there six waterpots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece. 7. Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim. 8. And He saith unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast. And they bare it. 9. When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not whence it was: (but the servants which drew the water knew;) the governor of the feast called the bridegroom, 10. And saith unto him, Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse; but thou hast kept the good wine until now. 11. This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth His glory; and His disciples believed on Him.’—JOHN ii. 1-11.

sermons.title: The First Miracle in Cana — The Water Made Wine
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xiv; heading #ii.xiv-p0.2 'THE FIRST MIRACLE IN CANA — THE WATER MADE WINE'
sermons.mainText: ‘This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth His glory.’—JOHN ii. 11.

sermons.title: Christ Cleansing the Temple
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xv; heading #ii.xv-p0.2 'CHRIST CLEANSING THE TEMPLE'
sermons.mainText: ‘Take these things hence; make not My Father’s house an house of merchandise.’—JOHN ii. 16.

sermons.title: The Destroyers and the Restorer
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xvi; heading #ii.xvi-p0.2 'THE DESTROYERS AND THE RESTORER'
sermons.mainText: ‘Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this Temple, and in three days I will raise it up.’—JOHN ii. 19.

sermons.title: Teacher or Saviour?
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xvii; heading #ii.xvii-p0.2 'TEACHER OR SAVIOUR?'
sermons.mainText: ‘The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto Him, Rabbi, we know that Thou art a Teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that Thou doest, except God be with him.’—JOHN iii. 2.

sermons.title: Wind and Spirit
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xviii; heading #ii.xviii-p0.2 'WIND AND SPIRIT'
sermons.mainText: ‘The wind bloweth where it listeth, and them hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.’—JOHN iii. 8.

sermons.title: The Brazen Serpent
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xix; heading #ii.xix-p0.2 'THE BRAZEN SERPENT'
sermons.mainText: ‘Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness.’—JOHN iii. 14.

sermons.title: Christ’s Musts
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xx; heading #ii.xx-p0.2 'CHRIST’S MUSTS'
sermons.mainText: ‘. . . Even so must the Son of Man be lifted up.’—JOHN iii. 14.

sermons.title: The Lake and the River
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxi; heading #ii.xxi-p0.2 'THE LAKE AND THE RIVER'
sermons.mainText: ‘God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life.’—JOHN iii. 16.

sermons.title: The Wearied Christ
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxii; heading #ii.xxii-p0.2 'THE WEARIED CHRIST'
sermons.mainText: ‘Jesus therefore, being wearied with His journey, sat thus on the well. . . . He said unto them, I have meat to eat that ye know not of.’—JOHN iv. 6, 32.

sermons.title: ‘Give Me to Drink’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxiii; heading #ii.xxiii-p0.2 '‘GIVE ME TO DRINK’'
sermons.mainText: ‘ . . . Jesus saith unto her, Give Me to drink . . . . Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am He.’—JOHN iv. 7, 26.

sermons.title: The Gift and the Giver
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxiv; heading #ii.xxiv-p0.2 'THE GIFT AND THE GIVER'
sermons.mainText: ‘Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith unto thee, Give Me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of Him, and He would have given thee living water.’—JOHN iv. 10.

sermons.title: The Springing Fountain
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxv; heading #ii.xxv-p0.2 'THE SPRINGING FOUNTAIN'
sermons.mainText: ‘The water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water, springing up into everlasting life.’—JOHN iv. 14.

sermons.title: The Second Miracle
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxvi; heading #ii.xxvi-p0.2 'THE SECOND MIRACLE'
sermons.mainText: ‘This is again the second miracle that Jesus did, when He was come out of Judaea into Galilee.’—JOHN iv. 54.

sermons.title: The Third Miracle in John’s Gospel
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxvii; heading #ii.xxvii-p0.2 'THE THIRD MIRACLE IN JOHN’S GOSPEL'
sermons.mainText: ‘Jesus saith unto him, Rise, take up thy bed, and walk.’—JOHN v. 8.

sermons.title: The Life-giver and Judge
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxviii; heading #ii.xxviii-p0.2 'THE LIFE-GIVER AND JUDGE'
sermons.mainText: ‘But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work. 18. Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill Him, because He not only had broken the Sabbath, but said also that God was His Father, making Himself equal with God. 19. Then answered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do: for what things soever He doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise. 20. For the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth Him all things that Himself doeth: and He will shew Him greater works than these, that ye may marvel. 21. For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom He will. 22. For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son: 23. That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son, honoureth not the Father which hath sent Him. 24. Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth My word, and believeth on Him that sent Me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life. 25. Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. 26. For as the Father hath life in Himself; so hath He given to the Son to have life in Himself; 27. And hath given Him authority to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man.’—JOHN v. 17-27.

sermons.title: The Fourth Miracle in John’s Gospel
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxix; heading #ii.xxix-p0.2 'THE FOURTH MIRACLE IN JOHN’S GOSPEL'
sermons.mainText: ‘And Jesus took the loaves; and when He had given thanks, He distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to them that were set down; and likewise of the fishes as much as they would.’—JOHN vi. 11.

sermons.title: ‘Fragments’ or ‘Broken Pieces’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxx; heading #ii.xxx-p0.2 '‘FRAGMENTS’ OR ‘BROKEN PIECES’'
sermons.mainText: ‘When they were filled, He said unto His disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.’—JOHN vi. 12.

sermons.title: The Fifth Miracle in John’s Gospel
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxxi; heading #ii.xxxi-p0.2 'THE FIFTH MIRACLE IN JOHN’S GOSPEL'
sermons.mainText: ‘So when they had rowed about five-and-twenty or thirty furlongs, they see Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing nigh unto the ship: and they were afraid. 20. But He said unto them, It is I; be not afraid.’—JOHN vi. 19, 20.

sermons.title: How to Work the Work of God
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxxii; heading #ii.xxxii-p0.2 'HOW TO WORK THE WORK OF GOD'
sermons.mainText: ‘Then said they unto Him, What shall we do, that we might work the works of God? 29. Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye, believe on Him whom He hath sent.’—JOHN vi. 28, 29.

sermons.title: The Manna
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxxiii; heading #ii.xxxiii-p0.2 'THE MANNA'
sermons.mainText: ‘I am that bread of life. 49. Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead. 50. This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.’—JOHN vi. 48-50.

sermons.title: One Saying with Two Meanings
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxxiv; heading #ii.xxxiv-p0.2 'ONE SAYING WITH TWO MEANINGS'
sermons.mainText:
‘Then said Jesus unto them, Yet a little while am I with you, and then I go unto Him that sent Me. 34. Ye shall seek Me, and shall not find Me: and where I am, thither ye cannot come.’—JOHN vii. 33, 34.
‘Little children, yet a little while I am with you. Ye shall seek Me; and as I said unto the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; so now I say to you.’—JOHN xiii. 33.

sermons.title: The Rock and the Water
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxxv; heading #ii.xxxv-p0.2 'THE ROCK AND THE WATER'
sermons.mainText: ‘In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto Me, and drink. 38. He that believeth on Me, as the Scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.’—JOHN vii. 37, 38.

sermons.title: The Light of the World
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxxvi; heading #ii.xxxvi-p0.2 'THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD'
sermons.mainText: ‘ . . . I am the light of the world: he that followeth Me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.’—JOHN viii. 12.

sermons.title: Three Aspects of Faith
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxxvii; heading #ii.xxxvii-p0.2 'THREE ASPECTS OF FAITH'
sermons.mainText: ‘Many believed on Him. Then said Jesus to those Jews which believed on Him . . . .’—JOHN viii. 30, 31.

sermons.title: ‘Never in Bondage’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxxviii; heading #ii.xxxviii-p0.2 '‘NEVER IN BONDAGE’'
sermons.mainText: ‘We . . . were never in bondage to any man: how gayest Thou, Ye shall be made free!’—JOHN viii. 33.

sermons.title: One Metaphor and Two Meanings
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xxxix; heading #ii.xxxix-p0.2 'ONE METAPHOR AND TWO MEANINGS'
sermons.mainText:
‘I must work the works of Him that sent Me, while it is day: the night cometh when no man can work.’—JOHN ix. 4.
‘The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light.’—ROMANS xiii. 12.

sermons.title: The Sixth Miracle in John’s Gospel — The Blind Made to See, and the Seeing Made Blind
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xl; heading #ii.xl-p0.2 'THE SIXTH MIRACLE IN JOHN’S GOSPEL—THE BLIND MADE TO SEE, AND THE SEEING MADE BLIND'
sermons.mainText: ‘When Jesus had thus spoken, He spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and He anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay, 7. And said unto him, Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent). He went his way, therefore, and washed, and came seeing.’—JOHN ix. 6, 7.

sermons.title: The Gifts to the Flock
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xli; heading #ii.xli-p0.2 'THE GIFTS TO THE FLOCK'
sermons.mainText: ‘ . . . By Me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture.’—JOHN x. 9.

sermons.title: The Good Shepherd
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xlii; heading #ii.xlii-p0.2 'THE GOOD SHEPHERD'
sermons.mainText: ‘I am the Good Shepherd, and know My sheep, and am known of Mine. 15. As the Father knoweth Me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down My life for the sheep.’—JOHN x. 14, 15.

sermons.title: ‘Other Sheep’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xliii; heading #ii.xliii-p0.2 '‘OTHER SHEEP’Preached before the Baptist Missionary Society.'
sermons.mainText: ‘Other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear My voice; and they shall become one flock and one Shepherd.’—JOHN x. 16 (R.V.).

sermons.title: The Delays of Love
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xliv; heading #ii.xliv-p0.2 'THE DELAYS OF LOVE'
sermons.mainText: ‘Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus. When He had heard therefore that he was sick, He abode two days still in the same place where He was.’—JOHN xi. 5, 6.

sermons.title: Christ’s Question to Each
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xlv; heading #ii.xlv-p0.2 'CHRIST’S QUESTION TO EACH'
sermons.mainText: ‘ . . . Believest then this? She saith unto Him, Yea, Lord.’—JOHN xi. 26, 27.
sermons.notes: subtitle printed under heading: 'For the Young'

sermons.title: The Open Grave at Bethany
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xlvi; heading #ii.xlvi-p0.2 'THE OPEN GRAVE AT BETHANY'
sermons.mainText: ‘Now Jesus was not yet come into the town, but was in that place where Martha met Him. The Jews then which were with her in the house, and comforted her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up hastily and went out, followed her, saying, She goeth unto the grave to weep there. Then when Mary was come where Jesus was, and saw Him, she fell down at His feet, saying unto Him, Lord, if Thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, He groaned in the spirit, and was troubled, And said, Where have ye laid him? They say unto Him, Lord, come and see. Jesus wept. Then said the Jews, Behold how He loved him! And some of them said. Could not this Man, which opened the eyes of the blind, have caused that even this man should not have died! Jesus therefore again groaning in Himself, cometh to the grave. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it. Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto Him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days. Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God? Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Jesus lifted up His eyes, and said, Father, I thank Thee that Thou hast heard Me. And I know that Thou hearest Me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that Thou hast sent Me. And when He thus had spoken, He cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go. Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on Him.’—JOHN xi. 30-45.

sermons.title: The Seventh Miracle in John’s Gospel — The Raising of Lazarus
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xlvii; heading #ii.xlvii-p0.2 'THE SEVENTH MIRACLE IN JOHN’S GOSPEL — THE RAISING OF LAZARUS'
sermons.mainText: ‘And when Jesus thus had spoken, He cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, Come forth. 44. And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with grave-clothes; and his face was bound about with a napkin.’—JOHN xi. 43, 44.

sermons.title: Caiaphas
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xlviii; heading #ii.xlviii-p0.2 'CAIAPHAS'
sermons.mainText: ‘And one of them, named Caiaphas being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.’—JOHN xi. 49, 50.

sermons.title: Love’s Prodigality Censured and Vindicated
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xlix; heading #ii.xlix-p0.2 'LOVE’S PRODIGALITY CENSURED AND VINDICATED'
sermons.mainText: ‘Then Jesus, six days before the passover, came to Bethany, where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom He raised from the dead. There they made Him a supper; and Martha served: but Lazarus was one of them that sat at the table with Him. Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped His feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment. Then saith one of His disciples, Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, which should betray Him, Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor? This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein. Then said Jesus, Let her alone: against the day of My burying hath she kept this. For the poor always ye have with you; but Me ye have not always. Much people of the Jews therefore knew that He was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom He had raised from the dead. But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death; because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.’—JOHN xii. 1-11.

sermons.title: A New Kind of King
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.l; heading #ii.l-p0.2 'A NEW KIND OF KING'
sermons.mainText: ‘On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, took branches of palm-trees, and went forth to meet Him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord. And Jesus, when He had found a young ass, sat thereon; as it is written, Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt. These things understood not His disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of Him, and that they had done these things unto Him. The people therefore that was with Him when He called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record. For this cause the people also met Him, for that they heard that He had done this miracle. The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing! behold, the world is gone after Him. And there were certain Greeks among them that came up to worship at the feast: The same came therefore to Philip, which was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and desired him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus. Philip cometh and telleth Andrew: and again Andrew and Philip tell Jesus, and Jesus answered them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of Man should be glorified. Verily, verily, I say unto you, except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit. He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal. If any man serve Me, let him follow Me; and where I am, there shall also My servant be: if any man serve Me, him will My Father honour.’—JOHN xii. 12-26.

sermons.title: After Christ: With Christ
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.li; heading #ii.li-p0.2 'AFTER CHRIST: WITH CHRIST'
sermons.mainText: ‘If any man serve Me, let him follow Me; and where I am, there shall also My servant be.’—JOHN xii. 26.

sermons.title: The Universal Magnet
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lii; heading #ii.lii-p0.2 'THE UNIVERSAL MAGNET'
sermons.mainText: ‘I, if I be lifted up . . . will draw all men unto Me.’—JOHN xii. 32.

sermons.title: The Son of Man
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.liii; heading #ii.liii-p0.2 'THE SON OF MAN'
sermons.mainText: ‘ . . . Who is this Son of Man?’—JOHN xii. 34.

sermons.title: A Parting Warning
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.liv; heading #ii.liv-p0.2 'A PARTING WARNING'
sermons.mainText: ‘Jesus therefore said unto them, Yet a little while is the light among you. Walk while ye have the light, that darkness overtake you not: and he that walketh in the darkness knoweth not whither he goeth. While ye have the light, believe on the light, that ye may become sons of light.’—JOHN xii. 35, 36 (R.V.).

sermons.title: The Love of the Departing Christ
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lv; heading #ii.lv-p0.2 'THE LOVE OF THE DEPARTING CHRIST'
sermons.mainText: ‘ . . . When Jesus knew that His hour was come that He should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved His own which were in the world, He loved them unto the end.’—JOHN xiii. 1.

sermons.title: The Servant-master
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lvi; heading #ii.lvi-p0.2 'THE SERVANT-MASTER'
sermons.mainText: ‘Jesus knowing that the Father had given all things into His hands, and that He was come from God, and went to God; He riseth from supper, and laid aside His garments; and took a towel, and girded Himself. After that He poureth water into a basin, and began to wash the disciples’ feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith He was girded.’—JOHN xiii. 3-5.

sermons.title: The Dismissal of Judas
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lvii; heading #ii.lvii-p0.2 'THE DISMISSAL OF JUDAS'
sermons.mainText: ‘. . . Then said Jesus unto Judas, That thou doest, do quickly.’—JOHN xiii. 27.

sermons.title: The Glory of the Cross
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lviii; heading #ii.lviii-p0.2 'THE GLORY OF THE CROSS'
sermons.mainText: ‘Therefore, when he was gone out, Jesus said, Now is the Son of Man glorified, and God is glorified in Him. If God he glorified in Him, God shall also glorify Him in Himself, and shall straightway glorify Him.’—JOHN xiii. 31, 32.

sermons.title: Cannot and Can
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lix; heading #ii.lix-p0.2 'CANNOT AND CAN'
sermons.mainText: ‘Little children, yet a little while I am with you. Ye shall seek Me: and as I said unto the Jews, Whither I go ye cannot come; so now I say to you.’—JOHN xiii. 33.

sermons.title: Seeking Jesus
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lx; heading #ii.lx-p0.2 'SEEKING JESUS'
sermons.mainText: ‘. . . Ye shall seek Me.’—JOHN xiii. 33.

sermons.title: ‘As I Have Loved’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxi; heading #ii.lxi-p0.2 '‘AS I HAVE LOVED’'
sermons.mainText: ‘A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another: as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are My disciples, if ye have love one to another.’—JOHN xiii. 34, 35.

sermons.title: Quo Vadis?
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxii; heading #ii.lxii-p0.2 'QUO VADIS?'
sermons.mainText: ‘Peter said unto Him, Lord, why cannot I follow Thee now! I will lay down my life for Thy sake. Jesus answered him, Wilt thou lay down thy life for My sake? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, The cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied Me thrice.’—JOHN xiii. 37, 38.

sermons.title: A Rash Vow
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxiii; heading #ii.lxiii-p0.2 'A RASH VOW'
sermons.mainText: ‘Jesus answered him, Wilt them lay down thy life for My sake? Verily, verily I say unto thee, The cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied Me thrice.’—JOHN xiii. 38.

sermons.title: Faith in God and Christ
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxiv; heading #ii.lxiv-p0.2 'FAITH IN GOD AND CHRIST'
sermons.mainText: ‘Let not your heart be troubled . . . believe in God, believe also in Me.’—JOHN xiv. 1.

sermons.title: ‘Many Mansions’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxv; heading #ii.lxv-p0.2 '‘MANY MANSIONS’'
sermons.mainText: ‘In My Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you.’—JOHN xiv. 2.

sermons.title: The Forerunner
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxvi; heading #ii.lxvi-p0.2 'THE FORERUNNER'
sermons.mainText: ‘. . . I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto Myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.’—JOHN xiv. 2, 3.

sermons.title: The Way
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxvii; heading #ii.lxvii-p0.2 'THE WAY'
sermons.mainText: ‘And whither I go ye know, and the way ye know. Thomas saith unto Him, Lord, we know not whither Thou goest; and how can we know the way? Jesus saith unto him, I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by Me. If ye had known Me, ye should have known My Father also: and from henceforth ye know Him, and have seen Him.’—JOHN xiv. 4-7.

sermons.title: The True Vision of God
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxviii; heading #ii.lxviii-p0.2 'THE TRUE VISION OF GOD'
sermons.mainText: ‘Philip saith unto Jesus, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us. 9. Jesus saith unto Him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known Me, Philip? He that hath seen Me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father? Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me? The words that I speak unto you I speak not of Myself: but the Father, that dwelleth in Me, He doeth the works. Believe Me that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me: or else believe Me for the very works’ sake.’—JOHN xiv. 8-11.

sermons.title: Christ’s Works and Ours
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxix; heading #ii.lxix-p0.2 'CHRIST’S WORKS AND OURS'
sermons.mainText: ‘Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on Me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto My Father. 13. And whatsoever ye shall ask in My name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. 14. If ye shall ask any thing in My name, I will do it.’—JOHN xiv. 12-14.

sermons.title: Love and Obedience
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxx; heading #ii.lxx-p0.2 'LOVE AND OBEDIENCE'
sermons.mainText: ‘If ye love Me, keep My commandments.’—JOHN xiv. 15.

sermons.title: The Comforter Given
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxxi; heading #ii.lxxi-p0.2 'THE COMFORTER GIVEN'
sermons.mainText: ‘And I will pray the Father, and He shall give you another Comforter, that He may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of Truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth Him not, neither knoweth Him: but ye know Him; for He dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.’—JOHN xiv. 16, 17.

sermons.title: The Absent Present Christ
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxxii; heading #ii.lxxii-p0.2 'THE ABSENT PRESENT CHRIST'
sermons.mainText: ‘I will not leave you comfortless; I will come to you. Yet a little while, and the world seeth Me no more; but ye see Me: because I live, ye shall live also.’—JOHN xiv. 18, 19.

sermons.title: The Gifts of the Present Christ
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxxiii; heading #ii.lxxiii-p0.2 'THE GIFTS OF THE PRESENT CHRIST'
sermons.mainText: ‘At that day ye shall know that I am in My Father, and ye in Me, and I in you. He that hath My commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth Me; and he that loveth Me shall be loved of My Father, and I will love him, and will manifest Myself to him.’—JOHN xiv. 20, 21.

sermons.title: Who Bring Christ
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxxiv; heading #ii.lxxiv-p0.2 'WHO BRING CHRIST'
sermons.mainText: ‘Judas saith unto Him, not Iscariot, Lord, how is it that Thou wilt manifest Thyself unto us, and not unto the world? Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love Me he will keep My words: and My Father will love him, and We will come unto him, and make Our abode with him. He that loveth Me not, keepeth not My sayings: and the word which ye hear is not Mine, but the Father’s which sent Me.’—JOHN xiv. 22-24.

sermons.title: The Teacher Spirit
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxxv; heading #ii.lxxv-p0.2 'THE TEACHER SPIRIT'
sermons.mainText: ‘These things have I spoken unto you, being yet present with you. But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in My name, He shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.’—JOHN xiv. 25, 26.

sermons.title: Christ’s Peace
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxxvi; heading #ii.lxxvi-p0.2 'CHRIST’S PEACE'
sermons.mainText: ‘Peace I leave with you, My peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.’—JOHN xiv. 27.

sermons.title: Joy and Faith, the Fruits of Christ’s Departure
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxxvii; heading #ii.lxxvii-p0.2 'JOY AND FAITH, THE FRUITS OF CHRIST’S DEPARTURE'
sermons.mainText: ‘Ye have heard how I said unto you, I go away, and come again unto you. If ye loved Me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father: for My Father is greater than I. And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye might believe.’—JOHN xiv. 28, 29.

sermons.title: Christ Foreseeing His Passion
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Ch. I to XIV (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.lxxviii; heading #ii.lxxviii-p0.2 'CHRIST FORESEEING HIS PASSION'
sermons.mainText: ‘Hereafter I will not talk much with you: for the Prince of this world cometh, and hath nothing in Me. But that the world may know that I love the Father; and as the Father gave Me commandment, even so I do. Arise, Let us go hence.’—JOHN xiv. 30, 31.

sermons.title: The True Vine
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ii; heading #ii.ii-p0.2 'THE TRUE VINE'
sermons.mainText: ‘I am the true vine, and My Father is the husbandman. Every branch in Me that beareth not fruit He taketh away; and every branch that beareth fruit He purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you. Abide in Me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in Me.’—JOHN xv. 14.
sermons.notes: misprint? heading reference 'JOHN xv. 14' disagrees with the book's contents list 'John xv. 1-4'

sermons.title: The True Branches of the True Vine
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iii; heading #ii.iii-p0.2 'THE TRUE BRANCHES OF THE TRUE VINE'
sermons.mainText: ‘I am the vine, ye are the branches: he that abideth in Me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without Me ye can do nothing. If a man abide not in Me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned. If ye abide in Me, and My words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you. Herein is My Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be My disciples.’—JOHN xv. 5-8.

sermons.title: Abiding in Love
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.iv; heading #ii.iv-p0.2 'ABIDING IN LOVE'
sermons.mainText: ‘As the Father hath loved Me, so have I loved you: continue ye In My love. If ye keep My commandments, ye shall abide in My love; even as I have kept My Father’s commandments, and abide in His love. These things have I spoken unto you, that My joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.’—JOHN xv. 9-11.

sermons.title: The Oneness of the Branches
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.v; heading #ii.v-p0.2 'THE ONENESS OF THE BRANCHES'
sermons.mainText: ‘This is My commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you. Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.’—JOHN xv. 12, 13.

sermons.title: Christ’s Friends
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.vi; heading #ii.vi-p0.2 'CHRIST’S FRIENDS'
sermons.mainText: ‘Ye are My friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you. Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of My Father I have made known unto you. Ye have not chosen Me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in My name, He may give it you. These things I command you, that ye love one another.’—JOHN xv. 14-17.

sermons.title: Sheep among Wolves
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.vii; heading #ii.vii-p0.2 'SHEEP AMONG WOLVES'
sermons.mainText: ‘If the world hate you, ye know that it hated Me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you. Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his Lord. If they have persecuted Me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept My saying, they will keep yours also.’—JOHN xv. 18-20.

sermons.title: The World’s Hatred, as Christ Saw It
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.viii; heading #ii.viii-p0.2 'THE WORLD’S HATRED, AS CHRIST SAW IT'
sermons.mainText: ‘But all these things will they do unto you for My name’s sake, because they know not Him that sent Me. If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloke for their sin. He that hateth Me, hateth My Father also. If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both Me and My Father. But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated Me without a cause.’—JOHN xv. 21-25.

sermons.title: Our Ally
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.ix; heading #ii.ix-p0.2 'OUR ALLY'
sermons.mainText: ‘But when the Comforter Is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, He shall testify of Me: And ye also shall bear witness, because ye have been with Me from the beginning.’—JOHN xv. 26, 27.

sermons.title: Why Christ Speaks
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.x; heading #ii.x-p0.2 'WHY CHRIST SPEAKS'
sermons.mainText: ‘These things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be offended. They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service. And these things will they do unto you, because they have not known the Father, nor Me. But these things have I told you, that, when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you of them. And these things I said not unto you at the beginning, because I was with you. But now I go My way to Him that sent Me; and none of you asketh Me, Whither goest Thou? But because I have said these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart.’—JOHN xvi. 1-6.

sermons.title: The Departing Christ and the Coming Spirit
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xi; heading #ii.xi-p0.2 'THE DEPARTING CHRIST AND THE COMING SPIRIT'
sermons.mainText: ‘Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send Him unto you. And when He is come, He will convince the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment.’—JOHN xvi. 7, 8.

sermons.title: The Convicting Facts
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xii; heading #ii.xii-p0.2 'THE CONVICTING FACTS'
sermons.mainText: ‘Of sin, because they believe not on Me; Of righteousness, because I go to My Father, and ye see Me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.’—JOHN xvi. 9-11.

sermons.title: The Guide into All Truth
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xiii; heading #ii.xiii-p0.2 'THE GUIDE INTO ALL TRUTH'
sermons.mainText: ‘I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. Howbeit when He, the Spirit of truth, is come, He will guide you into all truth: for He shall not speak of Himself; but whatsoever He shall hear, that shall He speak: and He will show you things to come. He shall glorify Me: for He shall receive of Mine, and shall show it unto you. All things that the Father hath are Mine: therefore said I, that He shall take of Mine, and shall show it unto you.’—JOHN xvi. 12-15.

sermons.title: Christ’s ‘Little Whiles’
sermons.book: Expositions of Holy Scripture: St John Chs. XV to XXI (CCEL)
sermons.locator: div id=ii.xiv; heading #ii.xiv-p0.2 'CHRIST’S ‘LITTLE WHILES’'
